name: Penang International Airport
before:
Penang's airport, at the south eastern tip of the island 16 km from George Town, and the main gateway to north western Malaysia. It carried over 7.6 million passengers in 2024, against a peak of 8.3 million in 2019 and an annual capacity of 6.5 million, so it is running above what it was built for.

It is the main hub for Firefly and one of AirAsia's operating bases. The route to Kuala Lumpur is one of the busiest air corridors in the country, and the link to Singapore Changi is the third busiest of Malaysia's ASEAN routes.

Freight matters more here than the size suggests. Penang handles the second largest cargo tonnage in Malaysia and the highest by export value, with RM365 billion of exports passing through in 2023.

Rapid Penang runs four bus routes between the airport and different parts of George Town.

The airport was completed in 1935 as Bayan Lepas International Airport, when Penang was part of the British Straits Settlements.
after:
Penang's airport is 16 km south of George Town. In 2024 it was Malaysia's second busiest airport for flights after KLIA, and it carried over 7.6 million passengers.

An RM1.5 billion expansion, due by 2028, will let the airport handle 12 million passengers a year.

Freight matters more here than the size suggests: Penang handles the second largest cargo tonnage in Malaysia after KLIA.

claims.note: The ministry's four 2024 quarterly tables give 1,763,597 + 1,898,369 + 1,981,411 + 1,998,248 = 7,641,625 (before transit). Its 2025 tables add up to 8,269,978, back at the 2019 peak, but no second source for 2025 was found, so the text keeps 2024.
